scope: Reviewed the final source diff and worker validation receipt for the historical Scala configuration-hash CI fix. This review does not qualify the Bifrost run or replace post-commit CI.

measurement_authority.assessment: The reviewed diff changes report-consumer history validation and its tests only. No benchmark driver, C5 source closure, runner, normalization, or measured-attempt evidence was changed.

verified: The four exact historical Bifrost versions (0.11.4, 0.12.0, 0.13.0, 0.13.1) hash only their policy closure; that branch does not open or hash the POM.

Bifrost 0.14.0 returns Current immediately only for an exact policy-only hash. Otherwise it checks the POM-inclusive hash, preserving the separately valid post-amendment profile without granting a general fallback.
Bifrost 0.14.4 and the pinned current version compare against the full policy-plus-POM closure; a legacy policy-only stamp cannot be accepted as Current.
Unregistered versions still reach an explicit error instead of inheriting a historical policy-only profile.
The production diff does not alter result normalization, benchmark execution, or dispatch logic.
tests_reviewed: The existing history test continues to cover all four retained legacy reports, the exact pre-amendment 0.14.0 hash, the POM-inclusive 0.14.0 hash, 0.14.4 full-hash acceptance, 0.14.4 legacy-hash drift, and unknown-version rejection.

The new child-process test runs from a minimal temporary root containing the Scala case and policy but no POM. It checks all four legacy exact hashes and mismatches, exact 0.14.0 legacy-hash acceptance, 0.14.4 missing-POM failure, and unknown-version rejection.
The child process avoids changing process-wide current directory in parallel Rust tests.
